backfill_note: The experiment ran on 2026-06-23 against DuckDB v1.5.3 (Variegata) + the quack core extension on a single Windows machine over loopback. Its harness (SQL scripts + the quack_serve invocation) lived in a gitignored tmp/ dir and was deleted after publish per the finite-disk firsthand policy. The harness here (server.sql + client.sql + run.sh) is reconstructed from the run's recorded methodology so a third party can reproduce the capability claims on the pinned DuckDB build. results.json holds the qualitative behavior matrix observed on 2026-06-23; re-running reproduces the same pass/fail / error-message outcomes. The latency numbers (Section 5) are machine-dependent context, never an evidence claim.

environment.extension: quack (autoloadable core extension: INSTALL quack; LOAD quack;)
environment.topology: single machine, loopback (client and server both DuckDB)
environment.note: This checks what a quack client-server session actually supports (auth, remote DML/DDL surface, transaction semantics, concurrent append, failure signalling). It is a capability/behavior check, not a timing benchmark; CPU/GPU/RAM do not affect the pass/fail matrix. Section 5 timings are localhost round-trip context only.

subject.name: DuckDB quack
subject.server: CALL quack_serve('quack:localhost', token := 'super_secret') -> http://localhost:9494 (localhost-only by default)
subject.client: CREATE SECRET (TYPE quack, TOKEN '...'); ATTACH 'quack:localhost' AS remote;
subject.status: beta in v1.5.3; stable target v2.0 (2026-09)
subject.note: quack turns the in-process OLAP DuckDB into a client-server pair where both ends are DuckDB. Autoloads from the network on first INSTALL quack.

environment_trap.note: On Windows, localhost binds to IPv6 ::1, so Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 9494 (IPv4) is a false negative. The client resolves quack:localhost the same way, so the session works despite the probe failing.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: harness discarded post-publish (finite-disk policy); reconstructed here
raw_artifacts.note: No large or binary artifacts. The deterministic evidence is the capability/behavior matrix in results.json (auth outcomes, remote DML surface, ROLLBACK non-propagation, concurrent-append survival, server-down signalling), re-derivable by running server.sql + client.sql on the pinned DuckDB build. Section 5 latency (remote agg ~0.5s, 1M transfer ~1.0s) is recorded as context only.
